newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JONES TRANSFORMS RAW TALENT INTO WORLD GOLD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JONES TRANSFORMS RAW TALENT INTO WORLD GOLD.

text.p: Marion Jones transformed raw talent into a world championship gold medal on Sunday at the start of what promises to become a new era for American sprinting.

On an unexpectedly cool, cloudy evening, Jones and Maurice Greene clinched the first U.S. 100 metres double in six world championships and the first at any global competition since the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
Jones, who returned to athletics this year after a successful college basketball career, defeated Ukrainian Zhanna Pintussevich by the thinnest of margins to win the women's title in 10.83 seconds.
Pintussevich, convinced she had won, danced along the track and was halfway down the backstraight when Jones was officially awarded the race.
"I thought I had got her but then she started celebrating," Jones said. "Then I looked over and some of my American team mates gave me the thumbs up."

Jones, who has a chance of two further titles in the long jumps and 4x100 metres relay, is the most exciting sprinter-long jumper to emerge from the United States since Carl Lewis announced his presence at the 1983 world championships.
Lewis was the last American man to win a major 100 title before Greene's triumph on Sunday, a fact which was not lost on the new world champion.
"I am an American and that's what I came here for, to get the gold medal for the United States," Greene said.
The American champion, consistency itself through the opening rounds, clocked 9.86 seconds in defeating defending champion Donovan Bailey. Only Bailey and Leroy Burrell have ever run faster.
Bailey took silver while Tim Montgomery confirmed the American resurgence with third place as Ato Boldon, the pre-race favourite after clocking 9.87 in the second round on Saturday, faded to fifth.

The only other title of the night, watched by a disappointingly small crowd, went to Heinz Weis in the hammer. The 34-year-old German saved his best for the final round when he recorded 81.78 metres, emitting a mighty roar as he threw the hammer into the night.
"I nearly lost my voice but it was worth it," he said.

Russia's 800 and 1,500 metres women's champion Svetlana Masterkova hobbled out of the championships after pulling up in the final straight of the 1,500 semifinals while defending champion Derrick Adkins was eliminated from the 400 metres hurdles.
Michael Johnson nearly preceded his American team mate when he eased up too soon in the second round of the 400 metres, finished fourth and missed automatic qualification to Molnday's semifinals.

After an anxious wait, Johnson qualified as one of the fastest losers, saving the world governing body the embarrassment of changing its rules to allow the world's best known athlete to take part and then losing him in the early rounds.
The double Olympic champion was granted a wild card to compete after missing the U.S. trials through injury.
